about: Every measurement taken of a model answering for the app's chatbot, copied from the notes of the day it was taken (each run names its source). A number that was not measured is null. `fit` is what the measurements say about offering the model for that job; `fitNote` is the sentence to tell somebody choosing.

machines.what: The stronger computer on the church's network: a desktop PC with one 8 GB graphics card (an RTX 3060 Ti, by the report of the session run on it), one model loaded at a time. LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, llamafile and GPT4All were all run on it; the app was driven from the laptop.
The same desktop PC with the model on its processor instead of its graphics card (GPT4All was run that way).
The developer's Windows ARM64 laptop, with no graphics card for a model: the CPU does the work. It drove the app in every run.

rules.rule: The app's own request is about 13 400 tokens before a word of the question (system prompt + tool schemas), and it is read again every round. A model loaded under 16k is refused before a round; at 16k a follow-up runs out of room; load with 32k.
rules.source: .claude/memory/custom-llm-servers.md — "The fixed request is ~13 400 tokens … CUSTOM_CONTEXT_MIN is 16k … every sentence recommends 32k"

rules.rule: A custom (local) server is sent a lean tool set — 14 of 26 tools, 4 234 tokens of schemas a round instead of 8 322 — because a local server pays for every schema in prompt-processing TIME.
rules.source: .claude/rules/chatbot-llm.md — "A custom server is sent 14 of those 26 … 4 234 tokens of schemas a round instead of 8 322"

rules.rule: On a computer with no graphics card the number that decides is how fast the PROMPT is read, not how fast the answer is written: at 11 tokens a second the app's request is a twenty-minute round and the 10-minute clock runs out; a graphics card reads about 1 000 tokens a second.
rules.source: .claude/memory/custom-llm-servers.md — "prompt processing is 11 tokens/s on qwen3.5:4b (2 335 tokens in 206 s) … a twenty-minute round on the 4B, and the SDK's 10-minute clock ran out"; "the user's LM Studio box reads ~1 000 tokens/s"

rules.rule: The program matters as much as the model on a slow computer: the same 4B model file was read at 11 tokens a second by Ollama and at 52.6 by llama.cpp's own server on the same laptop.
rules.source: docs/test-paths/coverage-matrix.md (CB-89) — "10 226 prompt tokens read in 194 s (52.6 tokens/s) on round 1 … Ollama's runner read the same file at 11 tokens/s"

rules.rule: A general question typed after /btw is the road for a slow computer or a small model: a ~60-token prompt, one round, no tools, and not held to the 16k rule.
rules.source: .claude/memory/chatbot-builtin-commands.md — "under a SHORT system prompt of its own (~60 tokens) … ONE round, NO tools … NOT refused by a custom server's 16k context rule"

rules.rule: A thinking model can spend its whole answer budget (2 000 tokens, thinking included) on thinking and return no words. A general question's thinking is switched off on LM Studio and Ollama, and an answer that came back empty is asked for once more with thinking off.
rules.source: .claude/rules/chatbot-llm.md and .claude/memory/custom-llm-servers.md — "A general question's thinking is OFF on LM Studio and Ollama"; backlog EC-201 — "the custom budget is MAX_TOKENS 2 000, thinking included"

rules.rule: One tool-using round in the app's request shape, on the server PC, by program: llama.cpp 20 s with the model's load at 45.6 tokens a second, Ollama 43 s with the load, llamafile 1.6 s at 67.7 tokens a second — all three made the right tool call. GPT4All's API server takes no tools at all (400), so its answers come from the guide text alone.
rules.source: docs/test-paths/coverage-matrix.md (ST-76) — "llama.cpp 20 s with the load at 45.6 tok/s, Ollama 43 s with the load, llamafile 1.6 s at 67.7 tok/s"; .claude/memory/custom-llm-servers.md — "GPT4All's API server takes no `tools` at all"

rules.rule: An 8 GB graphics card holds a 4B or 9B model with room for its context; a 12B barely fits it with a 16k cache.
rules.source: .claude/skills/owa-enhance-chatbot/references/backlog.md (EC-211) — "a 12B barely fits 8 GB with a 16k cache"

rules.rule: Through a Cloudflare tunnel a request whose answer has not started within 100 seconds is ended. The app asks a custom server for a whole answer at once, so a slow round fails there where it works on the local network.
rules.source: extra-work/local-llm/README.md (Worth knowing); measured by the session on the server PC, 2026-10-10

rules.rule: A free model must be driven through the REAL loop on several questions before it is listed — a one-tool ping passes models that then return empty answers under the full schema. Free models are differently broken, not merely weaker.
rules.source: .claude/memory/free-keyless-chatbot-provider.md — "Before listing a model, drive it through the REAL loop"; "Free models are differently BROKEN, not merely weaker"

models.name: Qwen 3.5 9B
models.fitNote: Answers app questions correctly through the tools in 20–30 seconds on an 8 GB graphics card. Load it with 32k: at 16k a first question fits and a follow-up runs out of room (it then writes its tool call as words, or no answer).
